utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, would you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I'd like to say good afternoon to all the parties and the witness as well, the Prosecution, the Defence, the accused, and everybody else. I have an oral decision, a brief one, to give you which regards BZ and the exhibits tendered. BZ appeared on the 9th of November, 2006. The Chamber has decided to admit all the exhibits presented and tendered by the Prosecution on the list IC 0085 [as interpreted], because they have certain probative value and relevance. I see that in the transcript there is a 0 missing. So it is IC 00085. Having said that, I would like to take the opportunity of saying that we have a witness for next week, and the Prosecution will be applying 92 ter procedure, which means that we should get through him rather quickly. The Chamber has deliberated and considers that the Defence will have approximately two hours for the cross-examination of that witness. Since you have already been informed of the fact that the Prosecution has asked for protective measures for the said witness, if there are no objections from the Defence, the Chamber will accord those protective measures for that witness as requested. We're going to start off with the testimony of this next witness within the frameworks of 92 ter. And without further ado, I give the floor to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. [In English] I'm going to proceed to read the summary of the statement, Your Honours. In 1993, the witness was 13 years old. He lived in the upper part of Sovici in the area called Kovaci. The village was attacked on the 17th of April, 1993. The shelling had started at 8.00, and a lot of grenades were landing very near the witness house. When the HVO took over Sovici, the villagers were ordered to go to the school building. In front of the school the soldiers were separated from the villagers. Women and children were taken inside the school while the men of military age were taken to an unfinished house nearby. On 18 April, 1993, when the witness was in the school building, he could see from the reflection on the windows that the Muslim houses were being set on fire. He heard a big explosion when the HVO soldiers blew up the mosque which exploded and fell to the ground. The witness later on passed by the destroyed mosque when he was taken out of the school by HVO soldiers to dig graves for -- to dig graves for them. Several days after the incident, women and children were sent to Juzunovici. The witness stayed in the building of the school along with 54 other Muslim men including elderly ones. One day, two unknown soldiers arrived to the school and called out four names and ordered them out of the school. Five minutes later, the witness heard four shots. One man who was in the -- in the school, looked out the window and he was taken out as well by the same soldiers. Later on, he heard another shot. These men never came back to school. HVO soldiers guarding the school physically mistreated detainees including the witness. The witness, along with other detainees, was taken to perform forced labour for HVO soldiers in the hills of Pisvir. They dug trenches for about three weeks there. In May, 1993, along with other Muslims from Sovici, the witness was transferred to Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: If I may. [Interpretation] I'm not quite sure what importance a summary is read out by the Prosecutor, as far as we've heard it, but if it does have any significance, except by way of a piece of information, I'd like to point out to the Trial Chamber that on page 2, the last paragraph of the witness statement, dated the 12th of March, 1999, the last sentence on that page, the witness expressly states that he didn't see anybody placing an explosive in the mosque. "All I saw was the mosque exploding and being set on fire." Now, a moment ago, my learned colleague said that the HVO soldiers must have been the perpetrators. This is not something we allow in criminal law. It is something that can be furthered in civil law, but I think that it is pre-emptive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Kovacic, are we to draw the conclusion that the mosque blew up all of its own accord?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. We will see from our exhibits and documents that the mosque was indeed blown up, but we do not know who blew it up. It could have been blown up by madmen. It could have been blown up by Muslims, Croats, members of the HVO, non-members of the HVO, people out of control, under control. There are various possibilities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Counsel, there are various possibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the burden of proof is on the Prosecutor, and I don't think -- and I wrote about this in my pre-trial brief. I don't think that the criteria of saying nobody else but them could have done it is just something that is unacceptable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. [In English] These are questions for cross-examination, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: It's just a summary for the purpose of the benefit of the public. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment. We were -- went very quickly and we forgot to have the witness take the solemn declaration. We're going to do that quickly now. For the transcript, would you give us your name, first name, last name, and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Nihad Kovac. I was born in December, the 15th of December, 1979.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And what is your profession at present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a driver by profession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Have you ever testified before an international or national tribunal, sir, about the events that took place in your village or is this the first time that you're testifying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a first time I'm a public witness, testifying publicly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now, independently of the fact that you were questioned by the investigators from the OTP, were you also questioned by investigators from your own country?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And do you know for what purpose, for what proceedings, before what judge and tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All I know is that it was in 1999 in Sarajevo that I was interviewed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Would you now read out the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since the Prosecution hadn't asked you any questions before you had taken the solemn declaration, you may now continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: So good afternoon, Mr. Kovac.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Do you remember being interviewed by someone from this Tribunal in the past?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Do you recall when?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Yes. And before the meeting you had yesterday, do you remember on the 12th of March, 1999, having given a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Do you remember -- did you answer the questions truthfully at that time?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And did you give your statement voluntarily?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: At the end of the interview, do you recall the statement being read back to you?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And it was read in your own language?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And do you recall signing that statement and saying that what you had said was the best of your knowledge and recollection?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown the hard copy of the statement bearing Exhibit Prosecution 9728.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: You have the opportunity to -- to read this statement before coming here to the Tribunal today?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And after reading the statement, do you recollect making some corrections to it?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signatures on the first page of the statement?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Is that your statement?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: If you go through the rest of the pages of the statement, could you -- could you see your initials there?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: In your statement, you have referred to the -- sorry. You have referred to the attacks of Sovici.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: You have referred, as well, to the troops that were involved in the attacks?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Do you remember which troops were those?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: The HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: All right. And in your statement you mentioned that the village was attacked by sort of fire artillery.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And you also mentioned that you were taken to -- afterwards to do forced labour at certain positions?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: I would like to put to the witness Exhibit 2 -- Prosecution 2009. Sorry, excuse me. 1 -- 1915. Yes, you can check there. This is an interim report dated 16th of April, 1993. If you go to the last page of it, at the end in your -- in your own -- in B/C/S, in B/C/S at the end, you have the name of a person. Could you please read it to me starting with Zeljko. At the end. At the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Zeljko Siljeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And on top of it, could you please read what it starts with "Forward post command".

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: It's barely legible on my copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Yeah. No problem. I will address you, then, to point 1 of that document. If you can look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor, the witness was 13 years old when the events took place. You're showing him a military document. "Forward command post," things like that mean nothing to him. Ask him about the pertinent paragraphs so that he can confirm them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Could you please address to point 2. Could you please read that one?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: "Establish a wire connection with facilities --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Witness -- perhaps I'm doing the same as you. Are you not, at present, living in the United States?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Would it not be quite as easy for you to do this in English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but if it was a better copy, more legible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Yes. I think that indeed there are no problems at all with the English version of this -- I'm sorry, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Trechsel. Mr. President, again, I fail to see the exercise of this -- the point of this exercise. We're having the gentleman read a document of which he had absolutely no contact with, no knowledge of. If we can get a narration perhaps from the witness, you know, and then maybe show the document and say does this verify. Otherwise, we're leading. I really cannot comprehend what kind of a trial this is turning into. I'm sorry, but I really don't understand this procedure. It's foreign to me. It's foreign in any system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: I will try to -- I will try to ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: You mentioned that you were taken to forced labour in the Pisvir elevations, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: All right. Where there were HVO troops?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Could you please read the English version, point 2.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: [In English] "Establish a wire connection with facilities Boksevica, Pisvir, Sovicka Vrata and with the command of the Mijat Tomic Battalion in the village -- Mijat Tomic Battalion in the village of Doljani."

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As a rule, Mr. Prosecutor, you should ask him this question, but I'm going to ask it. Now, it appears that in this military document, the word Pisvir figures. Is that the area, the place where you carried out forced labour that the soldiers wanted you to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There we have it. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: The following exhibit: 2009, Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Yes. In your statement, you mention that the houses in Sovici were set on fire, Muslim houses.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And you mentioned as well that there was a tank around the village after the attacks.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Could you please read this third paragraph of that starting with "Almost"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: For the convenience of the witness, Your Honour, we have no objection to the Prosecutor reading -- reading that section and asking the witness whether he can verify it. I think it might be a little bit more appropriate under the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Mr. Karnavas, for your contribution there. The Defence has understood it that we could move forward by you reading out the passage and then asking your question after that. We'll gain time that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: "Almost all the Muslim houses are set on fire in Sovici ..." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And during the attack or after the attack, did you see any internationals in the village, international observers?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: No. During the attack you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Yes. During the attack and after you were taken to the school.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: No. Except the HVO units, and I didn't know those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Next exhibit, 2052. This is a document signed by Marko Rozic, director of the Defence Department of Jablanica municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to speed up, this document, we've already referred to it. Counsel Nozica, I think, asked it not to be included, but the Chamber deliberated and the document will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: You see this document? This document --

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: -- defence department of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, bearing in mind that the exhibit will be admitted with the previous witness, then I think the Prosecutor has no need to ask questions about this document again. We're just wasting time, because you can't have this document tendered and admitted twice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Right. This document was admitted through another witness earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we'll move on to another document then. May we have Exhibit 2535.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: [In English] You have mentioned that the people were -- from military age, were assembled in Sovici and taken to Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Okay. And you mentioned as well that your uncle and father and some friends were taken there, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And under number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel Ibrisimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this is another document that we've already admitted. Yes. This document has been admitted, so there's no point in examining the witness on this. It's just a waste of time showing the same documents over and over again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document has already been admitted, so you can just give the names of his father and uncle and he can give you a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes I agree, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Kovac Ibro Ramo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: What about number 20? No, sorry. I withdraw.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: 63. Kovac, Ramo, son of Ibro. Is that your father?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: No, that's my uncle.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And at the end of the page, 106. Skender Nesir Armin?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: That's a friend. He was two years older than me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This document is related to the following one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: You -- I'm sorry. Just to make this clear. You say this friend of yours was two years older than you, so he was 15 years of age at that point; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And you also mention in your statement that your -- you also mention in your statement that your father was transferred to Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Exhibit 2546, Your Honours. It's a report from the military police regarding the 106 detainees that were -- that were transferred to Heliodrom and is related to the exhibit that was just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. In view of the contents of this document, which includes a lot of things, not only what the Prosecutor just said, I think it would be advisable to point out which passage is being indicated to the witness and how they will identify it, because from the previous document, we did see that maybe it's useful to ask him how many people there were, where they were going, et cetera, because he just identified his father and uncle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the -- the Prosecutor, you could say that this document mentions the transfer of so many persons headed for such-and-such a prison, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It is at the end of this document. 28th May, 1993. It is said that he got an order from Berko Pusic and Valentin Coric to transfer the prisoners to the Heliodrom prison. [In English] Now I will request to put to the witness Exhibit 7985.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And if you could please go to line -- point 36 and 37.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: That's my cousin and father -- uncle and father. That's my uncle.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And the person under it, 37?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: That's my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you please read that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Ibrisimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Not to waste time later, I have a couple of technical objections to this document of the military prosecution office in Mostar, whereby an exchange is agreed. If we look at the original on which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ibrisimovic, it will be better to voice your objections when you have the floor, and that will be very soon, because we believe that objections, technical, legal, or other, should be voiced during your cross-examination, and that will be the time to present your arguments.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... that four persons were taken out from the school in Sovici?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: What happened there?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Four men were taken out, four shots were heard. And after that, the fifth man who was taken out, looked through the window because in fact he didn't dare look outside and what was going on outside and what the shots were. They saw him looking through the window and that's when they took him out. After that, we heard another shot, and those men were never seen again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Could you please see Exhibit 8401 from the Prosecution. Do you remember one of the persons that were taken out that day from the school?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't know the names of the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the name, please?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Ismet Meho Cilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: For the record, it's in point 3 of the document, of the exhibit. Thank you very much. And if we can show Exhibit P 8625 to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Under point 10, is that the person you just mentioned to us?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Maybe the usher can assist. It's ERN 00740829. On the English version it's page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Point 10.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Is that the person you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You also mentioned in your statement that at one point you were transfer to Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Could you please look at -- one second. ERN number - the same document - 00740831. And in the English version, page 5. You have the number 450. Have you found it? No.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Okay. In your English version, page 5. The reference about the people being deported to Gornji Vakuf from Jablanica. Is that correct? From the village of Sovici.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I want to show you some pictures of the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor, there is no death certificate, because in your document, there should be a death certificate.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was an error with this death certificate, so we did not produce it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Exhibit 8952. Could it be displayed to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Do you see the -- do you see the picture on your screen? No. 8952. Yes. All right. If we can go to page with the ERN 9130. Do you recognise the village?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: What village is that one?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you show your house if it's on this picture? If you remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Maybe you can mark it there with that pen.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: That house should be here, but you can't see it, actually. The house is not there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Just mark the picture with your name on the side in the margin, the white margin. Registrar, a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit IC 000091.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: I would like to show now the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It might be useful to go on a bit with this picture which has such a nice general view. Witness, could you indicate the location where the mosque was?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: I was going there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: You have special pictures, I have seen it, but it's nice to have it in a general view, I think, if you don't mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the basis of this picture, could you indicate the location of the mosque maybe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mark it somehow distinctly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Approximately, the mosque is here. Here is the house of the hodja.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Put 1 above the circle denoting your house.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not a very good photo for this purpose. Maybe if you have another one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll work with this photo. Mark the mosque with a 2. And hodja's house with a 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: And is it possible to show approximately the situation, the location of the school on this picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Can we show the witness ERN number on same exhibit 9136. And before we continue with this photo, could request the registrar to give some CI number to -- it's an IC number, including the other two copies, marks in the photo. You have provided one for the first mark. Does this include the other two marks?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. The first photo marked with 1, 2, 3 we have numbers. So that's enough. Now we are going to have another IC number for the 36, which is still not on the screen. Madam Usher, we have to work very, very fast. We're waiting for the photo. Technology is good, but the old system is even better. Nothing can replace the ELMO. Mr. Karnavas seems to agree. So we can't have it. There is a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Could you please? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Do you recognise those two buildings?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... them?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes. This is hodja's house and the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And who was hodja?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Excuse me? Who was -- could you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: This is the house of someone living in front of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes. It's the hodja who was the imam of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And in your -- in your statement, you mentioned that you were taken by HVO soldiers to dig graves.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Can you please identify that place in the photo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, could you please mark the mosque with your pen there with 1. Put 2 next to imam's house. And then mark the place where you were digging graves with a 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Could you please sign the picture.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, can we have a number for this photo.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit IC 000092.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it's IC 00092.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... witness the photo under 9144 and 9145. Yes?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Do you recognise those houses there, those buildings?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: The one with the large red roof.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: It used to be the schoolhouse where we were detained, where I was held.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Could you please mark it with number 1.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: You mentioned that women and children were separated from men in front of the school and that men were taken somewhere else, and the children and the women and the elderly to the school.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Could you please mark the place where they were divided.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. For the record number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Put your name -- put your name there, please, again on the white margin.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, the number 2 should be mentioned so it goes on the transcript, otherwise, it won't be possible to tie them together later.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Yes. I was about to do that. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: For the record, number 2 is the place where the people were separated.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes. We were all there together. And this house marked by 2, that's where men were taken away from the basement, and we were on the parking lot. And from there, we were taken to the schoolhouse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, could we have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be IC 000093.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Petkovic. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I with like to ask the witness to mark the mosque on this photograph as well if it is visible, and the school. It would be nice to have a photograph of that kind which shows the view of the whole village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. The school and the mosque, do you see the mosque on this photo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. You cannot see the mosque. This is the central part of the village. The mosque is in the lower part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. And the school is marked by 1, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. So we can't see the mosque on this photograph. So the number is 000093.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: How far is the mosque from the school?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: About a kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And how could you see the mosque from -- from the school?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes. If you look -- if you look at the schoolhouse and if you open the windows, then you see everything from the top of the village where the mosque is located.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the basis of the photograph with this school on it, could you show in which direction the mosque is by drawing an arrow which starts from a school window. Just draw an arrow towards the mosque.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. And put there number 4. And on the margin, you have to write "Mosque," and thus everybody will understand that's where the mosque is, in that direction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does that accommodate the concerns of Mr. Petkovic? THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... of the -- of the school?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Well, roughly, it was two metres above the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Was -- could we show to the witness number 9150 of the same exhibit. Page 17 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. If I could ask for a clarification. It may just be that I'm slow this afternoon, but I'm not sure I understand the significance of the answer that the school was apparently two metres above the mosque. Is this referring to its elevation? Could we perhaps have a clarification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecutor asked you if the mosque was at the same level as the school and you said no, it was two metres above. Which is two metres above, the top of the mosque or the -- the foundation, the base of the mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I was trying to say is that -- that the mosque is maybe one or two metres higher than the school. The foundation, the base.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the base of the mosque is about two metres higher than the school.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I thought I understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... school was in the centre of the village, isn't it? That's what you said to us.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... mosque?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: The mosque is also kind of in the centre of the village. It's just that the village is conditionally divided into the lower part and the upper part, and the dividing line was somewhere between the school and the mosque.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a technical question. When we are standing in front of the school, do we see the mosque? Is it visible or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can see it from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Can we show then to the witness number 9150. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Could you recognise then the building?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the school where we were put up.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And you mentioned that you could see the house being set on fire and -- and the mosque from that school building?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Could you please mark with number 1 the place where you were in that school?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: So from that position you could see?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please put your name in the bottom corner. And a number, please, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit IC 000094.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And if -- if we can show to the witness ERN number 9157 of the same exhibit. 21 in the e-court system. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Do you see the picture?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: It's the window of the room we were in.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And when you mentioned that you could see the -- the mosque and the houses being burned, is that the -- the window you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So put a cross where the mosque was looking at it through the window, if you could see the mosque through the window. This view from the window, can you see the mosque or what was left of the mosque or the place where the mosque was? Can you see that looking out of the window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, you can't see the mosque, but if you open the window, then you can see the reflection from the mosque.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you open the window you can see the reflection of the mosque, but from that vantage point you can't actually see the mosque; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Looking through the window this way you can't see it. I would have to put my head through the window to see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. Now, when you were 13 years old, on the first floor of the school building, with your own eyes, did you see the mosque out of the window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you put your head out of the window, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I didn't see it with my own eyes. I told you I saw the reflection on the glass from window.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Your Honours. [Interpretation] The next photograph, Your Honour, shows the open window as the witness has just told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Show to the witness the following page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that photograph 57? Do you want it tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: I would request the registrar, please, to assign the number to it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit IC 000095.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, put your name -- place your name there, please. Next picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The number is 9158.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... first one. Yes. Do you recognise that picture?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: When you are referring that the window was open, is more or less this the situation?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Do you remember which part were you standing at the time you saw the houses being burned down?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Would you please mark it with number 1?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Yes. And number 1 is the place where the witness was standing when he was -- so when the houses were burning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Place your name and -- on the margin. Write your name in on the margin. And, Mr. Registrar, may we have a number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit IC 000096.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Witness, could you indicate in which direction the mosque would be as seen from this point inside the school? Maybe by drawing a -- yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And place a 2 by the arrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, the arrow drawn by the witness indicates the direction of the mosque as seen from the inside of the building, school building.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I ask the usher to turn to page 9164.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: In your statement you referred to the -- the fact that some people were divided and sent to Juzunovici.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Who else from your -- do you remember who was sent there?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: My sister, my mother was among them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And at one point you mention your statement that you were not allowed to join them, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: No, I couldn't go. I tried to get out up onto the truck but they took me down and sent me back.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And did you ever during that time went to Juzunovici?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes. I passed by once, jumped off the truck, but they sent me back two days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Do you remember the place where your family with the other people were interned, were arrested?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Could you please mark it with number 1?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: So for the record, number 1 is the place where the family of the witness and the civilians and children were interned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Put your name by the side. Number, please, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit IC 000097.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We have 20 more minutes to the break. Who is going to start off? The Defence has one hour. The Prosecution took one hour, so the Defence has one hour. Who is going to start off?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just have a couple of questions, if I could just ask them real quickly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. I guess my only question is, when you came here and you met with the Prosecution, did they go over these documents with you?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And did they go over the photographs with you as well?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In going over the documents, did they show to you the exact paragraphs they wanted you to look at and refer to in your testimony here today?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in looking at the photographs, did they also -- in going over them, did they point out or ask you to point out to them where the house was, the mosque was? Did they do that as well?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions. The purpose of the exercise, Your Honour, was at some point I will be making a request as to how to make the proceedings slightly more efficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. Counsel Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have just a few questions.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said in your statement that the village was attacked on the 17th of April, 1993; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, can you remember roughly -- and you just drew your own position in the school from which you saw the explosion of the mosque and the fire -- the houses set on fire. Can you tell us where that was in relation to the 17th of April, when that was?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps there's a mistake, Counsel Nozica. You said, "You saw the explosion." I understood it that he didn't actually see the explosion. He heard the explosion, not saw it. Witness, did you see the explosion or did you just hear the explosion? It's not the same thing. Which was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We heard the explosion. I couldn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you for that intervention.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Anyway, the explosion, when you heard it, when did you hear it and when did you see fire in Prozor in relation to the 17th April?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: I think it was the 18th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not Prozor, Counsel, it's his village.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I meant "prozor" meaning "window", through the window. Yes, it's the same word, "prozor", "window." So that's the misunderstanding in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So you said the 18th.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know when the men who, as you say were separated from the women, when they left? When did they leave the area? Can you remember that? Do you have that information?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You don't know? Can you remember what day you yourself, as you said in your statement, set out with the rest towards Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: We set out on the same day, the 17th, but we were returned from the village of Solde.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you tell us how you set off, who you set off with, and who sent you back?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: We set out with Mr. Dzemo Ovnovic in his van. Juka had agreed with Dzemo that we should go to Jablanica, the elderly and the women and children. We reached Solde, and the HVO soldier sent us back.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Although you talk about this in your statement, could you just tell us who Juka was?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: I don't know who he was and what he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Was Dzemo Vojinovic [as interpreted] a soldier?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And Juka, was he a soldier?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In your statement, on page 3, I think it's the English and Croatian version, you said the Croatian commander in Sovici called Juka, told Dzemo Ovnovic to take us to Jablanica. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Perhaps I did, but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Take a look at your statement. I don't know if you have it in front of you. In Croatian, on page 3. And for Their Honours' benefit, it is the second paragraph of page 3. It is the third paragraph in the B/C/S, in Croatian, and in English the second. Can you see that part?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It is the first paragraph on page 3 of the Croatian version of your statement. The first paragraph begins with: "Then they separated us and said that the old women and small children ..." Do see that? We're wasting a lot of time. I think you have page 3 in front of you. Can you see what I'm referring to?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It begins: "Then they separated us again." And it says, "The Croatian commander in Sovici, nicknamed Juka, told Dzemo Ovnovic ..." Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So which is it? Was he a Croatian commander? Did you know about that at the time?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: He was some sort of Croatian commander. Now, what he was exactly, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I realise that you were only 13 years old at the time and you didn't have to remember things like that, but since your statement has been admitted as an exhibit into evidence, it would be a good idea to clear this up, whether you knew this or whether this was introduced without your knowledge and was not corrected. So the Croatian commander told Dzemo Ovnovic to take you to Jablanica and go with him; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And then what happened? You came to Solde.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, and the HVO soldier stopped us in Solde and told Dzemo he couldn't pass through. He said he had a signature from Juka. And we were on our way to Jablanica, that he was supposed to transport the elderly women and children there. They started swearing and shouting. They said they had nothing to do with Juka and that we had to go back right away and that's what happened. We went back.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, please. At this same passage, in the English version it says, "We were stopped by Croat soldiers." I take it after hearing you now say that it was HVO soldier, that you did not want to make a point in your statement in saying that there were soldiers from the Croat army rather than from the Bosnia-Herzegovina HVO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I meant to say the HVO. I didn't mean soldiers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, counsel. Another question from the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Counsel Nozica. I have a question to ask, a point of clarification about commander Juka. Witness, you said that to begin with there were 30 soldiers with camouflage uniforms and bearing arms and that they weren't local soldiers. All right. That's that. Now, we come to this other Juka person. The soldier Juka, was he wearing the same uniform? Did he have any insignia? Was he a local soldier or not a local soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was an inhabitant, yes, a local, but he never wore any uniform. I never saw him in uniform at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. So there were two groups of soldiers. There were those who were wearing uniforms, about 30 of them you say, and then there was Juka who was a local, who was a soldier according to you, and who was a local commander; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but on that particular day, I didn't see him. I was told that by Dzemo while we were on our way in the van. Dzemo said that he had his signature and permit for us to go to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see. Thank you. Right. That shows that the investigators from the OTP weren't precise enough in taking the witness statement, because it doesn't quite correspond to the sentence as it reads in the statement. Thank you. Counsel Nozica, all that to show what? What do you wish to show? It's all very interesting, but what is the object of it?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, well, I'll explain, although I don't want to do this in front of the witness, but never mind, I will. The witness himself says that the Croatian commander ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness was 13 years old at the time, so he didn't know much.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. Precisely for that reason. However, the witness did say some things explicitly and it is my duty as Defence counsel to verify if he indeed remembers and whether things happened exactly as he said. He said that the Croatian commander in Sovici called Juka told Dzemo Ovnovic, and I believe this Trial Chamber knows who this is all about, that he should take some 15 people towards Jablanica. It transpires from the statement that they indeed set out for Jablanica. They were intercepted by soldiers. He says today those were HVO soldiers. And he told them that those were Juka's orders, but still they shouted at them and wouldn't let them through. My point is that everybody was issuing orders. Everybody was deciding depending on where one was. That is why I insisted so much on these details. May I move on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please say a word to the issue that you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead, although I didn't ask my question now.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Those HVO soldiers who came, the locals couldn't even bring bread, let alone have any other right. HVO soldiers wouldn't let them budge out of their houses, just as we weren't allowed to budge out of the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I don't see how it bears on my question, but let us move on. Could you please tell me, since we have dwelt for a while through documents as well on torched houses, at least you say they were torched, we read in your statement you saw Muslim houses set on fire. Can we know how long you observed this on this 18th through the window, how long it lasted, and what could you see? Could you just see the direction towards the mosque, or could you also observe other parts of the village from your vantage point inside the schoolhouse?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: It lasted all night, and I could see all those different parts through the -- in the window as a mirror.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: My question was: Could you just see one direction or more?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: I could see what I could see -- the houses burning, the houses that I could see through the window, not all the houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You mean the houses that were in the general direction of the mosque?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, my questions, as I would point out, concerning the 18th of April, were motivated by the fact that we have already heard some witnesses that testified a bit differently about this time and these events and the time when the mosque was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have just a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to follow up on what was just said. Witness -- Mr. Kovac, since you are not a protected witness, you just told my colleague on your own initiative, not related to her question, that HVO soldiers did not allow local people, not even to bring bread let alone leave their homes, and they didn't allow anybody to leave their home. My question is as follows: Does that mean that when the HVO troops entered the village, Croat residents were also in their homes and were not allowed to leave?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether they were in their homes or somewhere else, but I know, because I was informed as much, that none of the neighbours dared come near us. Nobody dared come near us except HVO soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. But did you know where the Croatian residents were at that moment?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you don't know whether they were at home, whether they maybe fled the village or did something else?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: No. I didn't see them that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about the whereabouts of the Croat population?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Kovacic. Witness, did you -- to whom did you refer? Who are you referring to when you say that people were not allowed to bring you food? Is it your idea that the Croats would have liked to come and bring you food, or were there, despite everything else we have heard, any Muslims left in the village, or any third type of persons? I hope I made myself clear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I heard later, a couple of days later, Croats tried to bring food, but that was hard. Local Croats tried to bring us food because we had neither bread nor water, but it was with great difficulty that they were allowed to bring anything if at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. In your statement that you confirmed at the beginning, you said you signed it and made it to the best of your knowledge and voluntarily. On page 2, passage 3, you said the following about the time before you were taken to the schoolhouse: You were in your home. You heard a bomb explode in the house next door. There were two or three families inside the house. You said there were about 20 people there. And then we find the sentence that I'm interested in. You said: "There were no soldiers among us or defenders of the village, and we did not have any weapons."

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's in the middle of the third paragraph on page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: What did you mean by saying that there were no defenders of the village? It was your house, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And where were the defenders of the village while you were taking cover indoors?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: What do you mean "defenders of the village"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Let me rephrase. Did anybody defend the village from the HVO, from the HVO raid?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: People who were more mature, of age, who wanted to defend their families.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Where were they, on the outskirts of the village?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Around the village. All those men left their homes at 8.00 a.m. in the morning when the shells started to fall, and they could not get to the top of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So is it fair to say they were at the edge of the village?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: No, you can't, because it was -- the edge is about 10, 15 kilometres of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So it's inside the village.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did they have anything prepared in advance like trenches, shelters, some sort of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did those men have weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How can we defend the village -- how can anybody defend the village without weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't see a single rifle. I didn't see anything. You can defend a village with an axe, with a shovel. At least that's what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And did you hear anything? You must have been curious as a boy. Did you hear that anybody had a weapon?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Let me rephrase this. Can you really claim under oath that nobody in the village had a weapon before that day when the conflict broke out?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that you don't know?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have only one small topic to cover within the framework of the document. It will be two or three questions. Maybe we can take the break now and I can finish after the break, or whatever you see fit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovac, you told us today you gave your first statement to OTP investigators on the 12th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Then on the 12th of January, 2001, you were invited to a meeting in Missouri, USA; correct?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And there you gave an affidavit.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: I don't understand the word "affidavit."

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Well, that's a statement under oath.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And in that statement you confirmed the previous statement that you gave in its English and Croatian versions. You confirmed it was indeed your signature, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And in this affidavit you gave in America, in paragraph 5, you said the following: "I understand that my statement attached to this affidavit may be admitted into evidence in proceedings before the International Criminal Tribunal, and I understand that false testimony under oath or a false statement constitutes a criminal act punishable by imprisonment or a fine. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And then in point 6, you confirmed the authenticity and the accuracy of the statement you had given previously. And in the last sentence you said expressly: "I have nothing to add to my statement, nor is there anything in this that I would like to change now." Correct?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And you signed that?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Then you arrived in The Hague a couple of days ago and you had a meeting with the Prosecution yesterday.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And, again, yesterday you went through the statement you gave in 1999.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: However, yesterday you explained, with regard to that statement, to the Prosecutor that you have minor corrections and modifications.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And you specified which?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, Your Honour, we have been duly informed by the Prosecutor, in keeping with your prior instructions, in a letter from the Prosecutor on 16 pages [as interpreted] of these modifications and corrections.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Witness, if in 2001, under oath, you stated that you had nothing to add to that statement in -- given in 1999, that it is absolutely correct and given to the best of your knowledge, nevertheless five years later when you came to The Hague you say, "I do have some corrections to make after all." What is the truth?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD KOVAC
utterances.text: Everything is the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I believe that you may have committed perjury, because in 2001 you said very loud and clear, "This is my statement. I have nothing more to add."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel, you are going too far. You are accusing this witness of perjury. What allows you to claim that? I remind you that he was 13 at the time. In 2001, he was 16. You are talking about an affidavit in Missouri. Where is that affidavit? I don't have it. Under what number?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose that the Prosecution duly provided it to the Chamber as one of his statements. That's one thing. Second, in January 2001, this witness was of age, and I absolutely agree with you that when he gave his first statement to the Prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you understood you were accused of false testimony. Now, explain to us, please, how come that in 2001 you specified certain points, you made certain statements? Did you lie, or did you just believe that some things that you have said before need to be further specified?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you have an explanation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then give it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that year, I think it was 2000, but I'm not sure, when I gave that statement in Missouri, I only read my statement and I said that it was correct, but at that time, I didn't know it would come to this and whether something would need to be added or not. Those -- those things that were added are just the same thing that was written before. It only brings more precision, more explanation. It's the same thing, just supplemented and expanded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But these corrections and -- and things that were made more specific, is it your decision or is it the Prosecution who told you that they needed to be made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. It was I who decided to add that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: May I -- I have two points. First, on page 43, first line, it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait a minute. He didn't answer the question. My question was very precise. You didn't answer, and my colleague wanted to intervene without realising that you had not answered yet. I asked you, when you made these modifications, did they come to you spontaneously, or was it the Office of the Prosecutor that suggested them? It's very simple. Please answer. Maybe you did answer, but it's not on the record.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I answered spontaneously. It was of my own will, of my own accord. I added it just in the same way that I replaced one word meaning "relative" with another more specific word meaning the same relation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now my colleague has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Yes. First a correction to the transcript. The translation said and it is written accordingly that Mr. Kovacic spoke of corrections of 16 pages, but I think you said 16 points, and it's not quite the same. So that should be corrected in the transcript. But, Witness, I would like to make an example. One of the new elements that you have said now is that not only the mosque but also the house of the imam was burned down. Now, when you made that affidavit in Missouri, were you aware of the fact that you had said in your statement that the mosque was destroyed, it was blown up, actually, and burned afterwards. And you knew exactly that also the house of the imam was burnt down, but you decided, "I will not say this although I'm aware of it". Was that what happened, or did you simply not think of it and only thought of it after you came here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I knew the hodja's house had been burnt at the same time that the mosque was blown up, but perhaps I forgot or it didn't come to mind to mention it. So that is why I made these additions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The affidavit, I know that procedure. You were in Missouri. How come -- how did it happen, the notary of the State of Missouri, Millford, called you -- did he call and say come over I have some things to ask you, or how did that whole thing come about? Do you remember? It was the 12th of January, 2001. How did it happen? Did they telephone you and tell you to come to the office of the person who was taking your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. They called me up on the telephone and asked me whether I agreed to give a statement for the public, and I said yes, and they said, "Can we come to America to meet and then you can confirm your statement?" And I said yes. And that's how we met, at one of the airports in Missouri.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And who did you meet at the Missouri airport?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember the name, but I do know that it was a lady who was speaking to me in Bosnian, and she spoke English as well. And the man, well, I don't remember what his name was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the man, it was an investigator from the OTP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We're going to take --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I have two or three more questions, but we can take a break if you prefer, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're going to take a break and reconvene at 4.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. But before I give the floor to Mr. Kovacic, I'd like, on behalf of the Chamber, to let you know, Mr. Kovacic, that of our indignation at raising what you did with the witness, especially as the Victims and Witness Unit told us about the traumatism caused to the witness. So if you have tangible proof, then produce that proof, and don't proceed with an assertion, because it's a very serious matter to state what you did. The Judges will not be intimidated. So bear that in mind. And we don't wish to upset the witness. And I think that your conduct was not intentional.
